basis: Congenital penile/preputial malformation is reproductive; urinary trapping does not establish intrinsic urinary tract damage.
Vaginal secretion is a reproductive finding; infection is one possible cause, not intrinsic to this concept.
Tumour originates in the posterior pituitary, an endocrine gland; common additional organ damage is not established.
B-lymphoblastic leukemia/lymphoma affects hematopoietic cells; the lymphoma component supports the immune mechanism axis.
Mandibular skeletal malposition defines the disorder; malocclusion follows the jaw abnormality. Craniosynostosis is occasional.
Arthrogryposis, femoral necrosis and gaze palsy define it; cardiac and pyloric defects each occur in 2/3. Asthma (3/3) omitted at the four-axis cap.
Carcinoma originates in the ectocervix, a reproductive organ outside the axes.
Carcinoma originates in breast parenchyma; spindle morphology does not establish skin or skeletal muscle origin.
Glycosylation disorder with cutis laxa and defining developmental brain disease; high myopia 80-99%. Joint laxity (11/12) and skeletal defects omitted at cap.
Mitochondrial disorder with defining encephalopathy; hearing loss 30-79%, muscle atrophy 1/2 with frequent weakness. Liver enzyme deficiency alone is not liver damage.
Optic atrophy defines it; mitral prolapse 3/5. Auditory abnormalities in 3/5 plus reported sensorineural hearing loss support ear involvement, with uncertain hearing-loss frequency.
Inherited rod-cone retinal degeneration with retinal atrophy and visual loss; no established extraocular damage in this concept.
Spastic paralysis, intellectual disability and retinal degeneration define the syndrome; infantile sensorineural hearing loss is frequent (30-79%).
Developmental brain disease, limb malformations and cleft palate are major features (80-99%); cataract, microphthalmia and coloboma occur in 30-79%. Heart damage unquantified.
Defective growth and osteonecrosis affect skeletal growth centres; unusual child concepts do not establish other organs across this umbrella.
Despite the susceptibility name, the definition specifies familial pancreatic carcinoma; exocrine pancreatic tumour origin is gastrointestinal.
The defining triad comprises intestinal aganglionosis, limb polysyndactyly and a ventricular septal defect.
Defining renal thrombotic microangiopathy causes kidney injury, hemolysis and thrombocytopenia; infection or autoimmunity is not universal across HUS.
Spastic paraplegia with motor and sensory neuropathy; persistent distal muscle atrophy occurs in 9/11 (~82%), supporting muscle involvement beyond weakness alone.
Congenital absence of the tricuspid valve is a structural heart defect.
Staphylococcus aureus infection directly inflames lung tissue; extrapulmonary complications are not established as common.
SCID with profound granulocyte/lymphocyte deficiency and defining congenital deafness (11/11); isolated hepatic and intestinal reports do not establish common direct injury.
Polypoid tumour arises in and occupies gastrointestinal mucosa.
Inherited adrenal steroid synthesis defect; reproductive manifestations have no axis, and common additional organ damage is not established.
Inherited photosensitive epilepsy phenotype reflects abnormal cerebral electrical responses; light sensitivity does not establish eye damage.
